title: Model Paper 1
html:
Sit this paper exactly as you will sit the real MECEE-BL: at a desk, with a watch, an OMR-style answer sheet (or a plain sheet ruled 1–200), a pencil and this book closed. Give yourself 3 hours (180 minutes) for the 200 questions — an average of 54 seconds each — and do not pause the clock.

Instructions, as the real paper gives them
  • Every question carries 1 mark. Four options; one is the best answer.
  • A wrong answer costs −0.25; a blank costs 0.
  • How to score yourself: count the right answers R and the wrong answers W, then your score is R − 0.25 W out of 200. Compare it with the 50th-percentile habit: in recent cycles a Group I merit place began around 120–140 — set your personal target above that and track it across the five papers.
  • Attempt strategy: sweep once through the questions you know (about 50 minutes a subject block), mark and return to the ones you can reason out, and never leave a question blank merely out of fear. From Chapter 1, a guess pays when your chance p of being right beats 0.2 (E = 1.25p − 0.25): killing two options earns +0.375 a guess, killing one +0.17, and even a blind four-way guess is mildly positive (+0.06) — but blind guessing swings the score, so reserve it for the last minutes.

Where the 200 questions sit

The area totals below are the official MEC weightage (third revision, 2083-01-15). The per-chapter split inside an area is the NEBians estimate used consistently by this book's subject volumes — every model paper in this book follows it question for question, so the five papers together rehearse the syllabus in its real proportions.
